assessment: Changes correlate with affected exports; causation and historical data availability remain unproved. These hypotheses convert disruption into control signals without establishing the success thresholds.

openings.claim: Use assignment and rename events to flag the affected center/week for course-set reconciliation. Potentially disruptive mutations become targeted warnings.
openings.delta: Maintain stable course identifiers in a private weekly manifest; request confirmation for changed courses before generating the documented CSV.
openings.prediction: Event-assisted reconciliation catches omitted intended courses in fabricated reassignment and rename cases, while unchanged cases require no added review.
openings.probe: Replay identical fabricated weeks through current selection and event-assisted reconciliation; compare intended identifiers and review time. Include splits, center-isolation checks and attendance entry during preparation.
assumptions: Mutation capture and manifests fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Failure boundary: missing past events, ambiguous splits or incorrect confirmation prevent reliable reconstruction.
Data remain private and center-authorized; recording and review do not block attendance entry.

openings.claim: Convert a missing-course report into an explicit center/week selection correction and immediate regeneration request: detected failure supplies the replacement export's selection control.
openings.delta: Replace an unstructured request with an authorized course picker and remembered weekly selection, avoiding unchanged reruns of a possibly defective selector.
openings.prediction: Explicit corrections produce usable replacements sooner; handling time improves only if identifying and confirming corrections is sufficiently cheap.
openings.probe: Have consenting coordinators repair fabricated mismatches using both workflows across their two sessions. Measure checking, correction, download and import separately; verify intended courses, documented CSV, concurrent entry and tenant boundaries.
assumptions: Private authorized regeneration fits six engineer-days and existing hosting.
Failure boundary: stale timetables, absent identities or ambiguous splits undermine corrections; the picker must never widen center access.
The 40–75 second job duration does not establish end-to-end replacement latency.
